Every section of the workshop has a notebook. One more sits past the end of the
day, as a take-home deep dive. They are **English-primary**, and every heading
carries a one-line Spanish summary — *cada encabezado lleva un resumen en
español.*

## How they are built

<span data-language-key="how-they-are-built"></span>

Notebooks 01–11 separate the live session from later study:

1. **Header:** **Practise today** and **Explore later**, with the same outcomes as the slides and handbook.
2. **Contiguous core block:** recall, example, attempt, feedback, checkpoint. Preparation and feedback definitions appear where needed. Work straight down.
3. **Core complete:** keep your explanation and follow the facilitator’s quiz and break schedule.
4. **Explore later:** optional reference material, exercises, and explorers.

Notebook 00 keeps the entry check and pre-work setup; 12 starts with the exit check. Notebooks 13–15 are take-home deep dives. Solutions remain folded: open them after an attempt. Each notebook loads its own data and runs independently.

::: {.callout-important appearance="simple"}
The notebooks are committed with **no outputs and no execution counts**. Every
number you see is one you produced. The prose quotes the expected results, so
you can tell whether yours are right. If yours differ, that is worth
investigating rather than dismissing.
:::

## Going further

<span data-language-key="going-further"></span>

These are **not sections**. They are deep dives, handed out as take-home
material. They have no slides, no Kahoot, and no minutes on the workshop clock:
the {{< var workshop.minutes >}}-minute agenda is exactly what it was without
them. 14 and 15 pick up where section 11 stops — section 11 fits CP as one of
four methods and calls the library deliberately as a black box; these two fit it
by hand and then change what "fit" means.

{{< include _includes/notebooks-extra-en.md >}}

## Running them somewhere other than Colab

<span data-language-key="running-them-somewhere-other-than-colab"></span>

The notebooks only need the scientific Python stack. Locally:

```bash
git clone {{< var repo.url >}}.git
cd {{< var repo.name >}}
uv run --group notebooks jupyter lab
```

The `notebooks` group is declared in `pyproject.toml`, and it is read off the
notebooks' own imports rather than written down beside them. `matplotlib` and
`ipywidgets` are in it because every notebook plots, and every one now builds
widgets — the thirteen that carry sliders, and 00, whose only widget is its
predict-first cell. Both ship with Colab, so a missing one only shows up when
you run locally.

`scikit-learn` and `scikit-image` ship the tumour data, the handwritten digits
and the photographs. So notebooks 01, 03, 04, 06 and 13 run with no network at
all. The other nine download something the first time they run: a CSV from
GitHub, the storm video clip from Wikimedia, or the voice recording for
notebook 12's take-home E. The table below says which, notebook by notebook.
